x: In the 880 yards which followed, Alby Bird showed fine form in gaining first place with Frank Webb also scoring. Again in the 220 yards our sprinters were unable to make any headway, but this was again nullified as our boys, Tom Carter, Arthur Allum and Tommy Morrell, ran well to win the 2 Miles.

Alby Bird was our last man, and he could not be expected to give Halford (L.A.C.) and Barnes (Achilles) a start. Bird held his position, however, and was content to ease off in the finishing straight when third place was secure (South London H. were fourth) and first and second teams could not be overtaken.

Our runners were more to the fore in the handicap events; mainly due to the fact that we provided the larger portion of the entries, especially in the 880 yards, which was won by Alby Bird off 8 yards.
White was caught and passed by the Mitcham runner. Alby Bird went next and, running with fine judgment, soon overhauled his man, and sent L.
Dee, the Welsh "crack," went next, with Alby Bird in hot pursuit. The leader, however, was not to be caught and, running in strong style, increased his club's lead.

Alby Bird raced into the lead, with Pack following, and they finished in that order, with Leigh filling third and fourth places. We thus led easily on the track events, but some closer competition was seen in the field contests.

With the last event to be decided our chances of even sharing the shield were gone, and Thames Valley consolidated their lead by winning the 1 Mile medley relay. Alec White beat Alby Bird over the half-mile stage, and although Dick Michael ran well in the 440 yards leg, Les.
We had been promised a good race in the 880 yards, and so it proved. Alby Bird ran finely to win in time which equalled Tommy Scrimshaw's record of 1 min. 59 1-5 sec.
Keyworth, off 17 yards, proved the winner, with Alby Bird, off 12, second; and R.
In the latter, Alby Bird had a comfortable run over the last stage, Dee, the Welsh crack, preferring to take things easy when he saw Alby go off about 30 yds. in front of him.
Arthur Beaumont, Fred White, Dick Michael, Ted Stimpson, Percy Wright, Alby Bird, Joe Daly and George Murray are also frequent strollers, and now the prodigal Alf Taylor has returned to the fold.
Alby Bird was an easy winner of the 880 yards in what was rather slow time, but here we lacked a second runner and so lost a chance of picking up useful points.
Syd Jarlett strode round to keep our advantage and sent Alby Bird off with a winning margin, which the Mitcham man did not attempt to cut down.

…d place and Tom Morrell 6th, all our runners in this race scored points to put us in the lead. The 880 yards was won by Alby Bird, with Dick Michael second. They had a ding-dong struggle which took them well away from their field.…
The time was slow, due mainly to the rough track, but conditions were the same for everybody and our man is to be congratulated on his good running. In the 880 yards Alby Bird met his "bogey man," A.

Robertson, the English International, chased Tom home, but he lost ground each lap at the water jump, which was a very stiff one. In the 880 yards Alby Bird easily qualified for the final, with MacCabe of the L.A.C., as also did A.

It was one of Pack’s best runs to date and if he could only find something of a finish, I would back him against the best in the country. In the 880 yards Alby Bird ran his usual consistent race and although coming up against his “bogey” man, A.
Thus we gained another very valuable point and with the 880 yards next, we hoped for the best from Alby Bird. Wooderson made his first appearance in this race and as the field also included J.
In the Senior 100 yards Southgate proved too strong for us; but Alby Bird credited us with first place in the 880 yards, and Frank Webb ran a fine race, to gain third place in this event.

This served as an appetiser for the Senior 880 yards, in which Alby Bird (holder) went into the lead at once, with the rest closely behind. At the bell he showed us that he meant to retain his title, and spurted ahead to enter the final straight with a commanding lead to win in 2 min. 3sec.
This year we experimented with a 300 yards race, but entries were very poor, due mainly to holidays, and Alby Bird, off 10 yards, ran a good race to just beat Stan Blunden, off 6.

Warboys writes from Wallasey, Cheshire, and keeps fit by evening walks by the sea and week-ends in North Wales. Alby Bird, who has been out of touch for a while, writes from Bolton, where he is now living, having been de-mobbed.
Bill Snell is now back from overseas and has already been on the road. Alby Bird, with his wife and youngster, were welcome spectators at the Club Championship Meeting.
